response.query: What sample size and consent language are required for medical-record validation, what MOU elements do partner clinics need, and how will discrepancies be handled analytically?
response.answer: For medical-record validation, informed consent is typically required, sample size depends on study design, and MOUs should include roles, responsibilities, and data-sharing terms. Discrepancies are resolved through data audits and collaborative analysis.

results.title: Healthcare GLN Implementation Guideline
results.content: ### provides implementation guidance for those considering the use of the GS1 Global Location Number (GLN) in healthcare. This document provides implementation guidance for the use of the GS1 Global Location Number (GLN) in healthcare. Issues to address are who maintains the right to use the GS1 Company Prefix(es) and the GS1 identification numbers (e.g. Global Trade Item Numbers (GTINs), Global Location Numbers, (GLNs), Serial Shipping Container Code (SSCC)) assigned using the GS1 Company Prefix, when ownership of the product or company changes. GS1 Locatenet, a central directory of GS1 Global Location Numbers (GLNs), enables the matching of NSW Health Location GLN to receiving Trading Partner GLN. Realising the importance of identifying the location as accurately and precisely as possible, Charité University Hospital decided to implement GS1 Global Location Numbers (GLNs) for accounts/locations as an essential step in its efforts to fully support the adoption of healthcare supply chain standards. Fukui Hospital is the first hospital in Japan to use GS1 Global Location Numbers (GLNs) to identify each of its locations.
